trails.description: The balance between capturing the reader's interest and providing enough content to fill the pages.

Two fairies together plucked at the heartstrings of the Viennese people, plunging them into a deep infatuation with the female performers of the Dittarsdorf family ...

items.text: The Mind's Endoscope
Two invitations, from the founder of "The Circle," no less.
A precious opportunity—a rare and precious clue to the goings-on here.
Hofmann caresses the edges, sinking into a long silence.
The obedient assistant looks off into the far distance, awaiting the impending storm.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ... You know what happened. But under the Foundation's regulations, I must reiterate that the primary subject of this investigation has been changed to Heinrich.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: These two invitations are very useful. I'll tell the Field Agent Squad to act tomorrow night. Once Heinrich's identity is verified, we will detain him in the exhibit.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But I must remind you, Marcus.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: What you did today was a serious violation of the Field Mission Manual. And I have to report this to the headquarters.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: That island is not of this era. Everything about it is strictly confidential. You have crossed a line.
The mentor's tone was of a stern reproach. Not so inconsequential anymore.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Understood ...
Marcus's complexion turns deathly pale. Her mouth hangs open to speak several times but fails to make a sound.
If not for the wall, she might well have fallen over.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I know what you're thinking. We need to get closer to this group.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You might think that their ideas are closer to those of the headquarters, and therefore easier to work with compared to the Vienna branch.
Marcus finds herself surprised by her stay of execution.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You must know that Kakania is not our only source of information.
Hofmann turns away, intentionally avoiding the overeager eyes of her apprentice.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: On the one hand, Karl has given us a list. In principle, everyone on this list is useful. On the other hand, the branch has its own connections too.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: More importantly, it takes more than a conversation over tea to get people on the same side of a conflict.
The experienced investigator sighs, rubbing her forehead.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I'm worried you are not ready for this, Marcus.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: There is too much wickedness out there dressed in the skin of kindness. The most horrible atrocities are always committed for the most seemingly justified reasons.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Even at the headquarters, people are mired in power struggles and compromises.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Sorry, ma'am, I was naive ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: It'll be the Foundation's judgment call. If the information you've gathered outweighs the risks, you may be treated leniently.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, look at the street.
The Ring Road has a feeling of tranquility despite the evening bustle.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You're not the only one who wants to contribute to this place and its people. We come for peace, and many before us have tried to prevent foreseeable tragedies, only to cause greater tragedies.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The rules are there for a reason. Nothing in the manual was written out of imagination. Every one of them came from a mistake of the past.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: We are only here to observe.
Many well-dressed citizens pass by, enjoying their sunset strolls.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: This is Vienna in 1914. The birthplace of an enduring war and chaos, the Critical Point.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: It is a powder keg, and the slightest spark will set it off. Any action we take could have unfathomable consequences.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: That's why we advise extreme caution.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: This is our responsibility to this era.
Marcus follows her mentor's hand, gazing into the distance.
For the first time, she scrutinizes the city ahead of her in detail.
Here, countless lives, possibilities, and thoughts new and old collide ...
Would all this end in an instant beneath a curtain of rain?
Marcus nods, searching out a word of affirmation.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... I understand completely, Madam Hofmann.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I won't make the same mistake again.
Away from the Ring Road, others continue on their life's trajectory.
In Kakania's clinic, a slightly unorthodox treatment is about to begin.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Isolde? You look sad and pale, what happened?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Did something happen in the troupe? Or did those dreadful officials come back?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: No. I'm just ... a bit worried.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: You ... you entered a duel for my sake. Dear lord, the thought of you getting hurt breaks my heart.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Did Heinrich tell you that? He needs to keep his mouth shut.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Don't worry about me, Isolde. I fought for the ethics of the profession, and I'm ready to bear the consequences of my actions.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: That scum sold the secrets of hypnosis to the military. It's a treatment, not a means of interrogation!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: In the end, all is well! The duel didn't happen, and I'm here, unharmed. All thanks to that young missy from the Foundation.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: That young missy from the Foundation ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: The lady who just left? I bumped into her at the door.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: So you've seen her.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: She was at the Secession Building. You weren't there.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Did she give you any trouble? You told me that the Foundation was after you for a while because you didn't have a license.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I can help you, doctor. I can ask Mr. Karl to ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Eh? No need for that. We only just became friends.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Friends?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: You told me to stay away from the Foundation staff, but now you're making friends with them ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, she's different, dear Isolde! We met by chance. I gave her an invitation to the exhibit, so you'll see her there. I think you two will become best friends.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It would take all day to tell you everything. You're here for treatment. Let's not waste time on unimportant things.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Unimportant? Alright ...
Kakania coughs, trying to revert to her more professional guise.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You're a personal friend, Isolde, so I didn't want to give you therapy in the first place ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Be-because I'm not good enough, or sick enough, to be your patient?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No no no, because I'm not good enough. I wasn't properly trained, I don't have a medical license, or a degree! This is the cold, hard truth, and you're too important a friend to me.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But I can no longer watch you suffer from the horrible treatments those quacks gave you.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I may not have a license, but I have the knowledge and ethics that they don't. I never overcharge my treatment, nor sell unnecessary things to the patient, and I will never experiment on my patients!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Heh heh.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Your smile. So you agree with what I said about those psychiatrists and doctors!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Okay, then let's get to it!
Kakania spins her pen in an excited twirl, flipping open her treatment book.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Dr. Sigmund Freud wrote that repression of desires is one of the primary causes of hysteria.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You need to release these desires. I'll guide your memory to find the deeply hidden thoughts. Trust me and tell me everything during the session.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You'll suffer less from the repression, and your physical ailments, fainting and convulsions, will become less severe.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Cast off your shackles and trust in me. This first step is crucial.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I know tragedies in your family have affected you deeply. But I'm here to help you now.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If you have trouble putting thoughts into words, use this mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It reflects your inner thoughts, like a mind's endoscope. I cast an arcane skill on it to help your thoughts surface.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Look at it, and tell me what you see.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: My inner thoughts ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Yes, I won't hypnotize you, nor will I turn around and peek at the mirror. What's in there belongs to only you, we're just going to talk.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hypnosis is a therapy I most detest. It doesn't help you understand and rediscover yourself.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And if the dialogue isn't based on the full awareness and consent of both parties, it's pointless.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I see. I will do my best.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Do your best? Hah, relax, you're not on the job. Just turn around, look in the mirror, and tell me ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What do you see?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Uhm ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I see ... golden circles ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Theophil in his study, on his feet, his hand gesturing intensely in the air ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Ah, yes, I'm there too. I'm ...
Her voice becomes strange and sharp.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Odd. Why am I not here?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Doctor, is your mirror not working? It's not showing my reflection. No, no, this isn't right, I promised to do my best ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I was there, I must have been. I have to remember it. You prepared all of this for my sake, I mustn't disappoint you ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh no, she's stuck in her obsessive thoughts!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Isolde, please sit down and listen to my voice.
The actress, ignoring her doctor's warnings, forcefully grips the edge of the mirror.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Who am I? Where am I?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Hello, is anybody there? Who is me? I am who? Greetings. Hello?
The candles go out, and the room fills with an inexplicable breeze.
An incorporeal voice responds to her inquiry, invited in from the void.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The lost ghosts. The last time in the Secession Building ... Now I understand.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I have to get her to stop relying so much on her arcane power. Luckily, not completing my education is why I know a little bit of everything.
The doctor rushes to the full-sized mirror in the workshop, removing the gray cloths one by one.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: What are you doing, doctor? Is the session over?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Was it because I did something wrong? Did I mess up?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Nonsense, you were doing great! I just have to clean the room a bit.
A more intense flash fills the clinic, dispelling the damp and resentful darkness.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Shoo, go away! Mirrors are useless to ghosts!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Leave my patient alone, and never come back!
TO BE CONTINUED…
